newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai minister confirms no oil intervention.
newsitem.headline: Thai minister confirms no oil intervention.

text.p: Thailand will not intervene to control retail oil prices even though the baht float will definitely send the prices higher, a senior government minister said on Thursday.
Sompong Amornvivat, minister in the prime minister's office in charge of energy policy, told Reuters the government would let market forces determine prices.
However, he asked oil companies to raise prices only to reflect changes in the exchange rate and in stages to delay its effect on the public.
"The very high competition in retail business here will make it a bit difficult for profiteering. Consumers should not be panicked," he said.
"I don't think it is a good idea for the government to control oil prices in a free market environment," he said.
Sompong denied reports the government would force oil refineries to cut profit margins to keep prices down.
"We did ask oil companies to cut marketing margins if they could. But if it not, we are not going to force them," he said.
The marketing margin is the initial profit to be shared by refineries and retail stations. Market margins are around 60-90 satangs per litre.

Thailand will use money from a 1.3 billion baht government oil fund to only subsidise LPG prices which are still controlled by the government. The de facto baht devaluation forced the government to postpone its plan to float prices of the product, which is used mostly for cooking.
Thai financial authorities on July 2 scrapped the tightly controlled foreign exchange regime and allowed the baht to move under a managed float system.
The move was seen raising the cost of oil products by 25-30 satangs per litre.
Sompong said state-run Petroleum Authority of Thailand and Banchak Petroleum Plc, the leader in retail oil business, would set benchmarks for the market with their prices.
A senior official at PTT said the company would increase its retail oil prices by 15-20 satang across the board later this week.
